Main.sentence: John Paul Stevens (April 20, 1920 – July 16, 2019) was an American lawyer and jurist who served as an ___E:associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associate_justice_of_the_Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ from 1975 to 2010. At the time of his retirement, he was the second-oldest justice in the history of the ___E:U.S. Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court)___ and the third- ___E:longest-serving justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_justices_by_time_in_office)___ .

At the time of his death in 2019 at age 99, he was the longest-lived Supreme Court justice ever.   His long tenure saw him write for the Court on most issues of American law, including ___E:civil liberties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_liberties)___ , the ___E:death penalty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment_in_the_United_States)___ , government action, and intellectual property.

Despite being a registered ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ who throughout his life identified as a conservative,   Stevens was considered to have been on the liberal side of the Court at the time of his retirement.

Born in Chicago, Stevens served in the ___E:United States Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ and graduated from ___E:Northwestern University School of Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University_Pritzker_School_of_Law)___ .

After clerking for Justice ___E:Wiley Rutledge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley_Rutledge)___ , he co-founded a law firm in Chicago, focusing on ___E:antitrust law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_antitrust_law)___ .

In 1970, President ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ appointed Stevens to the ___E:United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Seventh_Circuit)___ .

Five years later, President ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ successfully nominated Stevens to the Supreme Court to fill the vacancy caused by the retirement of Justice ___E:William O. Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_O._Douglas)___ .

He became the senior associate justice after the retirement of ___E:Harry Blackmun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Blackmun)___ in 1994. After the death of Chief Justice ___E:William Rehnquist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Rehnquist)___ , Stevens briefly acted in the capacity of Chief Justice before the appointment of ___E:John Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Roberts)___ .

Stevens retired in 2010 during the administration of President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and was succeeded by ___E:Elena Kagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elena_Kagan)___ .

Stevens's majority opinions in landmark cases include Sony Corp. of America v. Universal City Studios, Inc. , Chevron v. Natural Resources Defense Council , Apprendi v. New Jersey , Hamdan v. Rumsfeld , NAACP v. Claiborne Hardware Co. , Kelo v. City of New London , Gonzales v. Raich , U.S.
Term Limits, Inc. v.
Thornton , and Massachusetts v. Environmental Protection Agency .
Stevens is also known for his dissents in Texas v. Johnson , Bush v. Gore , Bethel v. Fraser , District of Columbia v. Heller , Printz v. United States , and Citizens United v. FEC .
Stevens was born on April 20, 1920, in ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ ,  Chicago, Illinois, to a wealthy family.

His paternal grandfather had formed an insurance company and held real estate in Chicago, and his granduncle owned the ___E:Chas A. Stevens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chas_A._Stevens)___ department store.

His father, Ernest James Stevens (1884–1972), was a lawyer who later became an hotelier, owning two hotels: the La Salle and the ___E:Stevens Hotel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevens_Hotel)___ .

The family lost ownership of the hotels during the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression_in_the_United_States)___ , and Stevens's father, grandfather, and an uncle were charged with ___E:embezzlement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement)___ ; the ___E:Illinois Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Illinois)___ later overturned the conviction, criticizing the prosecution.
His mother, Elizabeth Street Stevens (1881–1979), was a high school English teacher.
Two of his three older brothers also became lawyers.

A lifelong ___E:Chicago Cubs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs)___ fan, Stevens was 12 when he attended the ___E:1932 World Series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_World_Series)___ between the Yankees and the Cubs in Chicago's ___E:Wrigley Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrigley_Field)___ , in which ___E:Babe Ruth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth)___ allegedly ___E:called his shot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth%27s_called_shot)___ .
Stevens later recalled: "Ruth did point to the center-field scoreboard.

And he did hit the ball out of the park after he pointed with his bat, so it really happened."  He also had the opportunity to meet several notable people of the era, including the famed aviators ___E:Amelia Earhart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amelia_Earhart)___ and ___E:Charles Lindbergh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Lindbergh)___ , the latter of whom gave him a caged dove as a gift.

The family lived in ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ , and Stevens attended the ___E:University of Chicago Laboratory Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Laboratory_Schools)___ where he graduated in 1937. He later attended the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ , where he majored in ___E:English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_studies)___ , was inducted into ___E:Phi Beta Kappa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa)___ ,  and graduated with highest honors in 1941.  While in college, Stevens also became a member of the ___E:Psi Upsilon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psi_Upsilon)___ fraternity.
He began work on his master's degree in English at the university in 1941 but soon decided to join the ___E:United States Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ .

He enlisted on December 6, 1941, one day before the ___E:attack on Pearl Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor)___ , and served as an intelligence officer in the ___E:Pacific Theater U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asiatic-Pacific_Theater)___ from 1942 to 1945.  Stevens was awarded a ___E:Bronze Star U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_Star_Medal)___ for his service in the codebreaking team whose work led to the downing of ___E:Japanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan)___ Admiral ___E:Isoroku Yamamoto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isoroku_Yamamoto)___ 's plane in 1943 ( ___E:Operation Vengeance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Vengeance)___ ).

He also earned the ___E:World War II Victory Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II_Victory_Medal)___ and later received the highest United States civilian award, the ___E:Presidential Medal of Freedom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom)___ , from former ___E:President Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .

Stevens married Elizabeth Jane Shereen in June 1942. Divorcing her in 1979, he married Maryan Mulholland Simon that December; that marriage lasted until Simon's death in 2015 following complications from hip surgery.
He had four children: John Joseph (who died of cancer in 1996),  Kathryn (who died in 2018), Elizabeth, and Susan.
With the end of World War II, Stevens returned to Illinois, intending to return to his studies in English, but was persuaded by his brother Richard, who was a lawyer, to attend law school.

Stevens enrolled in the ___E:Northwestern University School of Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University_School_of_Law)___ in 1945, with the ___E:G.I. Bill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I._Bill)___ paying most of his tuition.

Stevens graduated in 1947 ranked first in his class with a ___E:J.D. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ magna cum laude , having earned the highest ___E:GPA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPA)___ in the school's history.

After receiving high recommendations from several Northwestern faculty members,  Stevens served as a ___E:law clerk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_clerk_of_the_Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ to ___E:Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ justice ___E:Wiley Rutledge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley_Rutledge)___ during the 1947–48 term.

Following his clerkship, Stevens returned to Chicago and joined the law firm of Poppenhusen, Johnston, Thompson & Raymond (now ___E:Jenner & Block U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenner_%26_Block)___ ).

Stevens was ___E:admitted to the bar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admission_to_the_bar_in_the_United_States)___ in 1949. He determined that he would not stay long at the Poppenhusen firm after being docked his pay for the day he took off to travel to ___E:Springfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield,_Illinois)___ to swear his oath of admission.
During his time at the firm, Stevens began his practice in ___E:antitrust law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_antitrust_law)___ .

In 1951, he returned to Washington, DC, to serve as associate counsel to the Subcommittee on the Study of Monopoly Power of the ___E:Judiciary Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_the_Judiciary)___ of the U.S. ___E:House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ .

During this time, the subcommittee worked on several highly publicized investigations in many industries, most notably ___E:Major League Baseball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball)___ .

In 1952, Stevens returned to Chicago and, together with two other young lawyers with whom he had worked at Poppenhusen, Johnston, Thompson & Raymond, formed his own law firm: Rothschild, Stevens, Barry & Myers.
It soon developed into a successful practice, with Stevens continuing to focus on antitrust cases.

His growing expertise in antitrust law led to an invitation to teach the "Competition and Monopoly" course at the University of Chicago Law School, and from 1953 to 1955, he was a member of the ___E:Attorney General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Attorney_General)___ 's National Committee to Study Antitrust Laws. At the same time, Stevens was making a name for himself as a first-rate antitrust litigator and was involved in a number of trials.
He was widely regarded by colleagues as an extraordinarily capable and impressive lawyer with a fantastic memory and analytical ability, and authored a number of influential works on antitrust law.

In 1969, the Greenberg Commission, appointed by the ___E:Illinois Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Supreme_Court)___ to investigate ___E:Sherman Skolnick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherman_Skolnick)___ 's corruption allegations leveled at former chief justice ___E:Ray Klingbiel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Klingbiel)___ and then-current chief justice ___E:Roy Solfisburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Solfisburg)___ , named Stevens as its counsel, meaning that he essentially served as the commission's ___E:special prosecutor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_prosecutor)___ .

The commission was widely thought to be a whitewash, but Stevens proved them wrong by vigorously prosecuting the justices, forcing them from office in the end.  As a result of the prominence he gained during the Greenberg Commission, Stevens became the second vice president of the ___E:Chicago Bar Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bar_Association)___ in 1970.

Stevens's role in the Greenberg Commission catapulted him to prominence and was largely responsible for President ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ 's decision to appoint Stevens as a judge of the ___E:United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Seventh_Circuit)___ in 1970. His nomination was put forth by a former ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ classmate, Illinois Senator ___E:Charles H. Percy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_H._Percy)___ .

On November 28, 1975, President ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ ___E:nominated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomination_and_confirmation_to_the_Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ Stevens as an ___E:associate justice of the United States Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associate_justice_of_the_United_States_Supreme_Court)___ , to a seat vacated by ___E:William O. Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_O._Douglas)___ .

Again, it was Percy who suggested Stevens; the nomination was also strongly supported by Attorney General ___E:Edward Levi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Levi)___ , former president of the University of Chicago.

He was ___E:sworn into office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oath_of_office#Federal_judiciary_oaths)___ December 19, 1975,  after being confirmed 98–0 by the ___E:U.S. Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate)___ two days before.

When ___E:Harry Blackmun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Blackmun)___ retired in 1994, Stevens became the senior associate justice and thus assumed the administrative duties of the Court whenever the post of ___E:Chief Justice of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States)___ was vacant or the chief justice was unable to perform his duties.

Stevens performed the duties of chief justice in September 2005, between the death of Chief Justice ___E:William Rehnquist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Rehnquist)___ and the swearing-in of his replacement, ___E:John Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Roberts)___ , and presided over oral arguments on a number of occasions when the chief justice was ill or recused.

Also in September 2005, Stevens was honored with a symposium by ___E:Fordham Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fordham_Law_School)___ for his 30 years on the Supreme Court, and President Ford wrote a letter stating his continued pride in appointing him.

In a 2005 speech, Stevens stressed the importance of "learning on the job"; for example, during his tenure on the Court, Stevens changed his views on ___E:affirmative action U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affirmative_action)___ (which he initially opposed), as well as on other issues.
President Ford praised Stevens in 2005: "He is serving his nation well, with dignity, intellect and without partisan political concerns."
Additionally, he participated actively in questioning during oral arguments.

Stevens was elected a fellow of the ___E:American Academy of Arts and Sciences U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Academy_of_Arts_and_Sciences)___ in 2008.  That same year he was elected to the ___E:American Philosophical Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Philosophical_Society)___ .

On January 20, 2009, Stevens administered the ___E:oath of office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oath_of_office)___ to Vice President ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ at Biden's request.
It is customary for the vice president to be inaugurated by the person of their choice.

On April 9, 2010, Stevens announced his intention to retire from the Supreme Court;  he subsequently retired on June 29 of that year.  Stevens said that his decision to retire from the Court was initially triggered when he stumbled on several sentences when delivering his oral dissent in the 2010 landmark case Citizens United v. FEC .
Stevens said "I took that as a warning sign that maybe I've been around longer than I should."

Stevens retired on June 29, 2010, as the ___E:third-longest-serving justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Justices_of_the_Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States_by_time_in_office)___ in the history of the Supreme Court with 34 years and six months of service and just three days short of tying the tenure of the second-longest serving justice in history, ___E:Stephen Johnson Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Johnson_Field)___ , who had retired on December 1, 1897. The longest-serving justice is Stevens's immediate predecessor, Justice ___E:William O. Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_O._Douglas)___ , who served 36 .mw-parser-output .frac{white-space:nowrap}.mw-parser-output .frac .num,.mw-parser-output .frac .den{font-size:80%;line-height:0;vertical-align:super}.mw-parser-output .frac .den{vertical-align:sub}.mw-parser-output .sr-only{border:0;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);clip-path:polygon(0px 0px,0px 0px,0px 0px);height:1px;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px} 1⁄2 years and retired on November 12, 1975. He was the last sitting Supreme Court justice to serve on the ___E:Burger Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burger_Court)___ .

Stevens was also the second-oldest justice, at age 90 years and two months at retirement, behind ___E:Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Wendell_Holmes_Jr.)___ who retired at the age of 90 years and 10 months on January 12, 1932. On July 23, 2015, Stevens became the longest-lived retired justice, surpassing ___E:Stanley Forman Reed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Forman_Reed)___ who died at age 95 years and 93 days on April 2, 1980.

On June 26, 2015, Stevens attended the Court's announcement of the opinion in Obergefell v. Hodges , in which the Court ruled 5–4 that recognition of ___E:same-sex marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage)___ is protected under the Constitution's ___E:Fourteenth Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ .
When he was appointed to the Supreme Court, Stevens was a registered ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ .
In September 2007, he was a sitting Justice when he was asked if he still considered himself a Republican.

Stevens replied, "That's the kind of issue I shouldn't comment on, either in private or in public."  Stevens was generally considered to be one of the last-surviving ___E:Rockefeller Republicans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Republicans)___ .

___E:Abner Mikva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abner_Mikva)___ , a close friend, said that as a judge, Stevens refused to discuss politics. "He was more particular about it than a lot of them," Mikva stated.

In October 2018, Stevens said that ___E:Brett Kavanaugh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Kavanaugh)___ 's performance during ___E:his confirmation hearings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Kavanaugh_Supreme_Court_nomination)___ should disqualify him from serving on the Supreme Court, citing the potential for political bias.  Kavanaugh was nominated by Republican president ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ .
Shortly before Stevens' death in 2019, he said he was "not a fan" of Donald Trump, and when asked about Trump's effect on the country, he stated "I don't think it's been favorable."

On the ___E:United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Seventh_Circuit)___ , Stevens had a moderately ___E:conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States)___ record.
Early in his tenure on the Supreme Court, Stevens had a relatively moderate voting record.

He voted to reinstate ___E:capital punishment in the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment_in_the_United_States)___ and opposed race-based admissions programs, such as the program at issue in Regents of the University of California v. Bakke , ___E:438 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_438)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:265 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/438/265/)___ (1978).

However, on the more conservative ___E:Rehnquist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Rehnquist)___ Court, Stevens joined the more liberal justices on issues such as ___E:abortion rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion-rights_movements)___ , ___E:gay rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_by_country_or_territory)___ and ___E:federalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism)___ .

His ___E:Segal–Cover score U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segal%E2%80%93Cover_score)___ , a measure of the perceived liberalism/conservatism of Court members when they joined the Court, places him squarely on the conservative side of the Court.
However, a 2003 statistical analysis of Supreme Court voting patterns found Stevens the most liberal member of the Court.

President Ford expressed no regrets about Stevens's drift toward liberalism, writing in a 2005 letter to USA Today , "Justice Stevens has made me, and our fellow citizens, proud of my three decade old decision to appoint him to the Supreme Court."
Stevens's jurisprudence has usually been characterized as ___E:idiosyncratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiosyncrasy)___ .

Stevens, unlike most justices, reviewed petitions for ___E:certiorari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certiorari)___ within his chambers instead of having his ___E:law clerks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_clerk)___ participate as part of the ___E:cert pool U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cert_pool)___ and usually wrote the first drafts of his opinions himself;   when asked to explain why, he said: "I'm the one hired to do the job." He further explained that he continued to learn about cases and legal theories as he drafted his opinions and re-evaluates his positions on cases while writing.

He was not an ___E:originalist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Originalism)___ (such as ___E:Antonin Scalia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonin_Scalia)___ ) nor a pragmatist (such as Justice ___E:Stephen Breyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Breyer)___ ), nor did he pronounce himself a cautious liberal (such as Justice ___E:Ruth Bader Ginsburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bader_Ginsburg)___ ).

He was considered part of the liberal bloc of the Court starting in the mid-1980s, and was dubbed the "chief justice of the liberal Supreme Court",   though he publicly called himself a judicial conservative in 2007.

In Cleburne v. Cleburne Living Center , ___E:473 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_473)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:432 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/473/432/)___ (1985), Stevens argued against the Supreme Court's famous " ___E:strict scrutiny U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strict_scrutiny)___ " doctrine for laws involving "suspect classifications", putting forth the view that all classifications should be evaluated using the "rational basis" test as to whether they could have been enacted by an "impartial legislature".

In Burnham v. Superior Court of California , ___E:495 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_495)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:604 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/495/604/)___ (1990), Stevens demonstrated his independence with a characteristically pithy concurrence.

Stevens was once an impassioned critic of ___E:affirmative action U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affirmative_action)___ ; in addition to the 1978 decision in Bakke , he dissented in the case of Fullilove v. Klutznick , ___E:448 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_448)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:448 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/448/448/)___ (1980), which upheld a minority set-aside program.

He shifted his position over the years and voted to uphold the ___E:affirmative action U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affirmative_action)___ program at the ___E:University of Michigan Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Law_School)___ challenged in Grutter v. Bollinger , ___E:539 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_539)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:306 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/539/306/)___ (2003).
Stevens wrote the majority opinion in Hamdan v. Rumsfeld in 2006, in which he held that certain military commissions had been improperly constituted.

He also wrote a lengthy dissenting opinion in Citizens United v. FEC , arguing the majority should not make a decision so broad that it would overturn precedents set in three previous Supreme Court cases.

When reviewing his career at the Supreme Court in his 2019 book, The Making of a Justice: Reflections on My First 94 Years , Stevens lamented being unable to persuade his colleagues against the decision in Citizens United , which he described as "a disaster for our election law."
Stevens's views on obscenity under the ___E:First Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Amendment_of_the_United_States_Constitution)___ changed over the years.

He was initially quite critical of constitutional protection for obscenity, rejecting a challenge to Detroit zoning ordinances that barred adult theaters in designated areas in Young v. American Mini Theatres , ___E:427 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_427)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:50 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/427/50/)___ (1976), ("[E]ven though we recognize that the First Amendment will not tolerate the total suppression of ___E:erotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erotic)___ materials that have some arguably artistic value, it is manifest that society's interest in protecting this type of expression is of a wholly different, and lesser, magnitude than the interest in untrammeled political debate"), but later in his tenure adhered firmly to a ___E:libertarian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarianism)___ free speech approach on obscenity issues, voting to strike down a federal law regulating online obscene content considered "harmful to minors" in ACLU v. Ashcroft , ___E:535 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_535)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:564 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/535/564/)___ (2002).

Stevens authored the majority opinion in Chevron U.S.A., Inc. v.

Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc. , ___E:467 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_467)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:837 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/467/837/)___ (1984).
The opinion stands for how courts review administrative agencies' interpretations of their organic statutes.
If the organic statute unambiguously expresses the will of Congress, the court enforces the legislature's intent.

If the statute is unclear (and is thus thought to reflect a Congressional delegation of power to the agency to interpret the statute), and the agency interpretation has the force of law, courts defer to an agency's interpretation of the statute unless that interpretation is deemed to be "arbitrary, capricious, or manifestly contrary to the statute".
This doctrine is now generally referred to as " Chevron deference" among legal practitioners.

Unlike some other members of the Court, Stevens was consistently willing to find ___E:organic statutes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_statute_(United_States))___ unambiguous and thus overturn agency interpretations of those statutes. (See his majority opinion in Immigration and Naturalization Service v. Cardoza-Fonseca , ___E:480 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_480)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:421 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/480/421/)___ (1987), and his dissent in Young v. Community Nutrition Institute , ___E:476 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_476)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:974 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/476/974/)___ (1986).) Although Chevron has come to stand for the proposition of deference to agency interpretations, Stevens, the author of the opinion, was less willing to defer to agencies than the rest of his colleagues on the Court.

In Bush v. Gore , ___E:531 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_531)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:98 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/531/98/)___ (2000), Stevens wrote a scathing dissent on the Court's ruling to stay the ___E:recount of votes in Florida during the 2000 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election_recount_in_Florida)___ .
He believed that the holding displayed "an unstated lack of confidence in the impartiality and capacity of the state judges who would make the critical decisions if the vote count were to proceed".

He continued, "The endorsement of that position by the majority of this Court can only lend credence to the most cynical appraisal of the work of judges throughout the land. It is confidence in the men and women who administer the judicial system that is the true backbone of the rule of law. Time will one day heal the wound to that confidence that will be inflicted by today's decision.
One thing, however, is certain.
Although we may never know with complete certainty the identity of the winner of this year's presidential election, the identity of the loser is perfectly clear.
It is the Nation's confidence in the judge as an impartial guardian of the rule of law."

Heller ___E:554 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_554)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:570 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/554/570/)___ (2008), a ___E:landmark case U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_landmark_court_decisions_in_the_United_States)___ which addressed the interpretation of the ___E:Second Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ and the ___E:right to keep and bear arms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_keep_and_bear_arms)___ .

Heller ___E:struck down U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judicial_review_in_the_United_States)___ provisions of the ___E:Firearms Control Regulations Act of 1975 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firearms_Control_Regulations_Act_of_1975)___ and held that the Second Amendment protects an individual's right to possess a ___E:firearm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firearm)___ unconnected with service in a militia for traditionally lawful purposes, such as self-defense within the home. His dissent was joined by justices ___E:David Souter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Souter)___ , ___E:Ruth Bader Ginsburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bader_Ginsburg)___ , and ___E:Stephen Breyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Breyer)___ ; the majority opinion was written by Justice ___E:Antonin Scalia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonin_Scalia)___ .

Stevens stated that the Court's judgment was "a strained and unpersuasive reading" which overturned longstanding ___E:precedent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precedent)___ , and that the Court had "bestowed a dramatic upheaval in the law."  Stevens also stated that the amendment was notable for the "omission of any statement of purpose related to the right to use firearms for hunting or personal self-defense" which was present in the Declarations of Rights of ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_Constitution_of_1776#Declaration_of_Rights)___ and ___E:Vermont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Vermont_(1777))___ .

Stevens' dissent seems to rest on four main points of disagreement: that the Founders would have made the individual right aspect of the Second Amendment express if that was what was intended; that the "militia" preamble and exact phrase "to keep and bear arms" demands the conclusion that the Second Amendment touches on state militia service only; that many lower courts' later "collective-right" reading of the Miller decision constitutes stare decisis , which may only be overturned at great peril; and that the Court has not considered gun-control laws (e.g., the ___E:National Firearms Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Firearms_Act)___ ) unconstitutional.

The dissent concludes, "The Court would have us believe that over 200 years ago, the Framers made a choice to limit the tools available to elected officials wishing to regulate civilian uses of weapons. ...
I could not possibly conclude that the Framers made such a choice."

On March 27, 2018, days after the ___E:March for Our Lives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_for_Our_Lives)___ demonstrations in the wake of the ___E:Stoneman Douglas High School shooting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoneman_Douglas_High_School_shooting)___ , described by many media outlets as a possible ___E:tipping point U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tipping_point_(sociology))___ for ___E:gun control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control)___ legislation,    Stevens wrote an essay for The New York Times , stating that the demonstrators should be demanding the outright repeal of the Second Amendment.
He wrote:

Concern that a national standing army might pose a threat to the security of the separate states led to the adoption of that amendment, which provides that "a well regulated militia, being necessary to the security of a free state, the right of the people to keep and bear arms, shall not be infringed." Today that concern is a relic of the 18th century.

In 2011, Stevens published a memoir entitled Five Chiefs: A Supreme Court Memoir , which detailed his legal career during the tenure of five of the Supreme Court's ___E:chief justices U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States)___ .

In Five Chiefs , Stevens recounts his time as a law clerk during the tenure of ___E:Chief Justice Vinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_M._Vinson)___ ; his experiences as a private attorney during the ___E:Warren era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Court)___ ; and his experience while serving as an associate justice on the ___E:Burger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burger_Court)___ , ___E:Rehnquist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rehnquist_Court)___ , and ___E:Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberts_Court)___ Courts.

In 2014, Stevens published Six Amendments: How and Why We Should Change the Constitution , where he proposed that six ___E:amendments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_V_of_the_U.S._Constitution)___ should be added to the U.S.

Constitution to address ___E:political gerrymandering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerrymandering_in_the_United_States)___ , ___E:anti-commandeering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printz_v._United_States)___ , ___E:campaign finance reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campaign_finance_reform_in_the_United_States)___ , ___E:capital punishment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment_in_the_United_States)___ , ___E:gun violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_violence_in_the_United_States)___ , and ___E:sovereign immunity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_immunity_in_the_United_States)___ .
In 2019, at age 99 and shortly before his death, Stevens published The Making of a Justice: Reflections on My First 94 Years .

Stevens married Elizabeth Sheeren in 1942. He was on the high court when the couple divorced thirty-seven years later in 1979. Later that same year, he married Maryan Simon; they remained married until her death in 2015. Stevens had four children, two of whom predeceased him. Stevens was a ___E:Protestant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant)___ , and upon his retirement, the Supreme Court had no Protestant members for the first time in its history.

He was one of only two Supreme Court justices who divorced while on the Court—the first was ___E:William O. Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_O._Douglas)___ , whom he coincidentally succeeded as an associate justice.
Stevens was also an avid ___E:bridge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contract_bridge)___ player and belonged to the Pompano Duplicate Bridge Club Florida.
Stevens was a private pilot who owned and flew a Cessna 172 with the registration number N1688F for almost two decades.
On July 16, 2019, Stevens died at the age of 99 at a hospital in ___E:Fort Lauderdale, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida)___ , from complications of a stroke.
He received hospice care and was with his two surviving children, Elizabeth and Susan, when he died.

He ___E:lay in repose U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lying_in_repose)___ at the Supreme Court on July 22, 2019  before a planned burial at ___E:Arlington National Cemetery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery)___ the following day. The service was attended by all the justices on the court, as well as retired justices ___E:Anthony Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Kennedy)___ and ___E:David Souter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Souter)___ .
President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ ordered flags to fly at half-staff as a mark of respect on Tuesday, July 23, until sundown.

According to an April 2009 article in The Wall Street Journal, Stevens "rendered an opinion on who wrote ___E:Shakespeare's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare)___ plays," proclaiming himself an ___E:Oxfordian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfordian_theory_of_Shakespeare_authorship)___ .
